project.name: mini-coding-agent
project.objective: Build the minimum working, provider-agnostic Engineering Agent described in the attached System Design Document and Iteration 1 Technical Implementation Plan

lifecycle.next_action: Review completed work and choose the next bounded outcome.

assumptions.text: Iteration 2 evaluation tasks (§52-§58) require a live LLM provider (Claude or Gemini). The baseline comparison is a best-effort run, not a blocking gate — consistent with how Iteration 1 treated live evaluation (AC-12 required a recorded success rate, not 100%). Evaluation results are recorded in eval/iteration2/ but a failed evaluation run is analyzed, not a blocker to plan completion.

The existing Iteration 1 agent loop (src/agent/loop.ts) accumulates messages in a plain array and passes them directly to provider.generate(). Iteration 2 must refactor this to route through Context Manager. The refactor preserves all external behavior (AgentResult shape, logging events, CLI commands) while replacing the internal message-accumulation pattern. No breaking changes to public interfaces.
Iteration 3 planning: the request text "before starting Iteration 2 implementation" is read as Iteration 3 (Iteration 2 is complete and approved). Confirm at spec review.

This workspace is not a Git repository (no .git). RepositoryScope uses read-only "git check-ignore" (internal to the navigation layer, never agent-invocable) only when the target workspace is a Git repository; otherwise it uses the default exclusion list. Ignore-handling tests create temporary Git repositories.

No standalone ripgrep binary is installed on the development machine (rg exists only as a Claude Code shell function). Search and the find_symbol text fallback use rg when an executable rg is found and otherwise a built-in bounded scan with identical scope rules and result format. Tests cover both paths.

invariants.text: The Agent Loop must not import or depend on any specific LLM provider SDK (Gemini, OpenAI, Claude, etc.) directly. All provider-specific code is isolated inside provider adapters behind a provider-independent LLM interface.

The agent must not declare a coding task successful solely because the LLM produced a confident final message. Verification must run before completion, and the final result must clearly distinguish: changes made, verification performed, verification passed/failed, verification not performed, remaining uncertainty.

File tools are restricted to the configured workspace by default; paths outside the workspace are rejected unless explicitly permitted. Command execution passes through an explicit ALLOW/DENY/CONFIRM policy rather than unrestricted shell access. No automatic git push. No destructive operations by default.

The agent loop must never run forever: a configurable MAX_AGENT_ITERATIONS (default 20) stops the task with status=failed, reason=iteration_limit. Repeated identical/substantially-identical failed actions must be detected and stopped after a configurable threshold, reporting that the same failing action was repeated.

Messages sent to a provider must satisfy the tool-call pairing contract: every tool_result block sits in the message immediately after the tool_use it answers, and its toolCallId must match an id in that preceding assistant message. Validating message ROLES alone is insufficient - a reordered or partially-dropped history can place a tool_result after an assistant turn from a different iteration, which passes a role check and fails at the API with 'unexpected tool_use_id'. Compare ids.

Any ordering key for context items must be strictly monotonic, not a wall-clock timestamp. Date.now() has millisecond resolution and an assistant turn with its own tool result are stored microseconds apart, so they tie. A tie makes the comparator return 0 and a stable sort then preserves whatever upstream order it was given - which is the context builder's priority order, not chronological. The result is a tool_result placed before its own tool_use.

Derived configuration must have a single source of truth. The compaction trigger and the message-build budget must be computed from the same window value. Previously compaction fired at 22,323 tokens while the build budget was 195,904, so context was discarded with ~88 percent of the provider window still free.

decisions.title: Iteration 1 scope: 4 tools, single Gemini provider, TypeScript/Node
decisions.text: Iteration 1 MVP implements exactly 4 tools (Search, Read File, Edit/Write File, Run Command) behind a Tool Registry, a single Gemini provider adapter behind a provider-independent LLM Interface, a CLI entrypoint, an Agent Loop with iteration limits and repeated-failure protection, basic (non-RAG, non-compacted) context, structured logging, and an IMPLEMENTATION_PROGRESS.md checklist tracked throughout. Tech stack: TypeScript, Node.js, npm, tsx, vitest, zod, Gemini official SDK. No agent framework.

decisions.title: Evaluation requires independent verification, not agent self-report
decisions.text: A single successful run is insufficient; each of >=5 evaluation tasks must be run multiple times with independent verification (not trusting the agent's final message), success rate tracked, and failures classified into a fixed taxonomy (UNDERSTANDING, SEARCH, FILE_SELECTION, TOOL_SELECTION, TOOL_INPUT, CODE_CHANGE, TEST_INTERPRETATION, RECOVERY, CONTEXT, SAFETY, FALSE_SUCCESS, LOOP, PROVIDER).

decisions.title: Genesis is authoritative for progress tracking
decisions.text: Do not maintain a separate IMPLEMENTATION_PROGRESS.md checklist file as mandated verbatim by the Iteration 1 doc. Genesis's own task tracking (PLAN.md, project.json, genesis brief/status/context) is the single source of truth for resumability and progress, satisfying the same interrupted-agent-resume intent more rigorously than a hand-maintained markdown checklist.

decisions.title: Gemini API key supplied via environment variable by developer
decisions.text: The human has a Gemini API key and will export GEMINI_API_KEY themselves outside of chat/commits. Implementation reads GEMINI_API_KEY and GEMINI_MODEL from environment/.env (gitignored), never hardcoded or logged. Live evaluation tasks can proceed in Iteration 1.

decisions.title: Iteration 1 vertical slice: full loop plus one live evaluation task
decisions.text: The first approved Genesis plan covers: CLI, agent loop, all 4 tools (Search, Read, Edit/Write, Run Command), Gemini adapter, safety policy (workspace boundary + command allowlist), unit + integration tests, and exactly ONE real end-to-end evaluation task (calculator bug fix) proven across multiple repeated runs with independent verification. The remaining 4 evaluation tasks and the full cross-task failure-analysis framework are explicitly deferred to a fast-follow task/plan after the core loop is proven, not part of the first vertical slice.

decisions.title: Command safety policy: narrow allowlist, deny-by-default
decisions.text: Run Command tool ALLOWs only: npm test, npm run build, npm run lint, npm run <script-defined-in-package.json>, node <file-within-workspace>. Everything else (including npm install/ci, rm, git push, sudo, curl, chmod, and any command not matching the allowlist) is DENY by default. No CONFIRM tier in Iteration 1 -- ALLOW/DENY only, extensible later.

decisions.title: Edit/Write tool contract: whole-file write + exact string replace
decisions.text: The Edit/Write tool supports exactly two operations: 'write' (create or overwrite full file content) and 'replace' (find an exact old_string in the target file and replace with new_string; fails if old_string is not found exactly once). No line-number-based or fuzzy/patch-based editing in Iteration 1.

decisions.title: Default workspace root is process.cwd()
decisions.text: When the CLI is invoked without --workspace, the workspace root defaults to the current working directory at invocation time. All file/search/command tools resolve paths relative to and bounded by this root.

decisions.title: Run Command default limits: 30s timeout, 100KB output cap
decisions.text: Run Command tool defaults: 30 second timeout per command, 100KB combined stdout+stderr cap with truncation notice when exceeded. Both configurable via CLI flag/env var, falling back to these defaults.

decisions.title: IMPLEMENTATION_PROGRESS.md is NOT maintained in Iteration 2
decisions.text: iteration2.md §62 asks for IMPLEMENTATION_PROGRESS.md to track progress. This conflicts with the existing Iteration 1 constraint: Genesis (PLAN.md + project.json via genesis brief/status) is the sole source of truth for progress and resumability. No duplicate hand-maintained checklist file is maintained. Progress is tracked through Genesis task state.

decisions.title: Iteration 2 context token defaults and configurability
decisions.text: Default context budget: MAX_CONTEXT_TOKENS=32000, RESERVED_OUTPUT_TOKENS=4096, MAX_TOOL_OUTPUT_TOKENS=4000, MAX_FILE_READ_TOKENS=6000, COMPACTION_THRESHOLD=0.80. All configurable via environment variables without code changes. These are examples from iteration2.md §9; exact model-specific limits are supplied by the provider's ModelCapabilities. Core Context Manager uses the configured values, not hardcoded provider limits.

decisions.title: Deterministic compaction only in Iteration 2 first implementation
decisions.text: Iteration 2 uses deterministic structured summarization (Option A from §23): extract user task, modified files, commands, test results, important facts, errors. LLM-based summarization (Option B) is not implemented in Iteration 2. It may be an experiment in a future iteration. Rationale: predictable, testable, no extra LLM API cost per compaction.

decisions.title: Provider capabilities window drives compaction, not a fixed 32000 default
decisions.text: Supersedes the MAX_CONTEXT_TOKENS part of DECISION-0fa985d8. loadContextPolicy now accepts the provider's capabilities().contextWindowTokens as the default for maxContextTokens; 32000 remains only as a last-resort fallback when no provider window is known. An explicit MAX_CONTEXT_TOKENS env var still wins. Reason: compaction fired at 22,323 tokens while the build budget was the provider's full 195,904, discarding context with most of the window free and causing the agent to re-read files it had already read. Effect: compaction now fires at 156,723 tokens for Claude. NOTE: not yet exercised by any real run - no real-world run has crossed the new threshold.

decisions.title: edit_file 'operation' parameter is optional and inferred
decisions.text: Refines DECISION-42507f50. The tool still supports exactly two operations (write, replace), but 'operation' is no longer required: it is inferred from the payload (old_string present means replace, content present means write), and an explicit value is used only when it is one of the two valid strings. Removed from the schema's required list. Reason: models omit the discriminator because essentially no mainstream editing API has one, and they ignored the corrective error message three times in a row. Inference also absorbs synonyms (str_replace, create, overwrite) without a synonym table.

decisions.title: run_command allowlist widened to read-only shell utilities - NEEDS HUMAN REVIEW
decisions.text: MODIFIES DECISION-811bfc29 (deny-by-default, narrow allowlist of npm test/build/lint/run-script and node <file-in-workspace>). The allowlist now also permits: find, grep, ls, cat, wc, head, tail, echo, python, python3, npx. Reason: the agent could not explore a real workspace; 'find' was denied and the run failed immediately. Mitigation: commands run with shell:false and shell metacharacters (pipes, redirects, chaining, backticks, command substitution) are now rejected outright, so these cannot be composed into arbitrary shell. Residual risk NOT mitigated: 'cat' can read any file the process can reach including outside the workspace (unlike the file tools, run_command does not confine its arguments to the workspace root); python and python3 permit arbitrary code execution and effectively nullify deny-by-default; npx can fetch and execute remote packages. This was changed mid-session to unblock real-world usage and has NOT been reviewed against the Iteration 1 safety model. Iteration 3 should either confine run_command arguments to the workspace and drop python/npx, or explicitly accept the widened boundary.

decisions.title: Tree-sitter via web-tree-sitter (WASM) with tree-sitter-wasms grammars - PROPOSED, confirm at spec approval
decisions.text: Use the Node ecosystem: web-tree-sitter (latest 0.27.0) plus prebuilt grammars from tree-sitter-wasms (0.1.13), both pinned. Rationale: no native compilation on Node 26, no Python, and the grammar bundle already contains many languages (java etc.) so add-language needs no extra install. Task IMPL-IT3-6 begins with a spike gate proving parse of TS/JS/Python on the installed Node; if it fails, stop and ask the human before switching to native tree-sitter.

decisions.title: Extend existing search and read_file in place; snapshot Iteration 2 as the eval baseline
decisions.text: search and read_file keep their names and every existing parameter (query, path, filePattern, caseSensitive, maxResults; path, startLine, endLine); new parameters are additive (mode, contextLines). Because the repository has no Git history, IMPL-IT3-0 copies the Iteration 2 src tree to eval/iteration3/baseline-src/ before any change so the Iteration 2 baseline runs the original tools.

decisions.title: SymbolMatch.source is a three-value union
decisions.text: Source requirements conflict: section 12 lists "tree-sitter" | "text-search" while section 17 requires "tree-sitter+text-search". The type accepts all three; text-search matches are never labelled as declarations.

decisions.title: Ground-truth manifests are JSON, not YAML
decisions.text: The requirements example uses YAML but the project has no YAML parser and a standing no-new-dependency preference. Manifests carry the same fields (task, relevant_files, acceptable_files, verification.command) as JSON.

decisions.title: IMPLEMENTATION_PROGRESS.md is not adopted; Genesis ledger is the progress record
decisions.text: Same resolution as DECISION-0bdf962d for Iteration 2. The Iteration 3 checklist maps to Genesis tasks IMPL-IT3-*; .genesis/PLAN.md is the generated progress view.

decisions.title: Paid real-provider evaluation needs explicit human cost authorization - PROPOSED
decisions.text: Real-provider tasks (context test, 6 tasks x 5 runs x baseline and Iteration 3) incur API cost. They are isolated in IMPL-IT3-18 and IMPL-IT3-19, which must not start until the human states provider, model and a run/cost cap. Consistent with ASSUMPTION-c52062ad (live evaluation is analyzed, not a free gate).

decisions.title: find_symbol keeps the parameter name symbol_name as specified
decisions.text: The requirements document names the input symbol_name (snake_case) while existing tools use camelCase. The explicit requirement wins; no alias is added (YAGNI). Revisit if evaluation shows tool-selection confusion.

decisions.title: Iteration 3 real-provider evaluation uses Claude for now; system stays provider-agnostic
decisions.text: Human direction (2026-10-08): use Claude for the real-provider context test and evaluation runs; the system must remain model agnostic so other services can be added later. Consequences: evaluation code goes through the LLMProvider interface only (INVARIANT-5a5b83ad); the harness takes provider/model as parameters, not hard-coded; src/navigation and the harness import no provider SDK (NFR-14). Refines DECISION-8791b3de: provider is chosen, but a model name, run cap and cost limit are still required before IMPL-IT3-18/19 start.

decisions.title: web-tree-sitter pinned to 0.25.10, not 0.27.0 (grammar load failure)
decisions.text: Spike on Node 26.7.0: web-tree-sitter 0.27.0 and 0.26.13 fail to load every tree-sitter-wasms 0.1.13 grammar (getDylinkMetadata: grammars carry the legacy 'dylink' wasm section, newer runtime requires 'dylink.0'). 0.25.10 loads and parses TS, TSX, JS and Python cleanly with the same ESM named exports (Parser, Language); a missing grammar is a handled Error. Pin web-tree-sitter 0.25.10 and tree-sitter-wasms 0.1.13 exactly. Supersedes the version numbers in DECISION-8e437c98; the WASM approach itself is unchanged. Known limit: tree-sitter-wasms is unmaintained (last release 2024). Human approved this pin when asked at the spike-failure stop point.
decisions.source: IMPL-IT3-6 spike 2026-10-08; human answer in chat

decisions.title: IT3-19: add dollar meter/ledger to eval/iteration3/run.ts
decisions.text: User required a hard $1 budget for the 60 paid runs (2026-10-12). Edited eval/iteration3/run.ts (outside the task's declared scope eval/iteration3/results) and tests/unit/eval/harness.test.ts to add --max-cost-usd, a fetch-level meter and results/ledger.json. knowledge.title: Project purpose and learning objective
knowledge.text: Engineering Agent is an independent, provider-agnostic coding agent built to understand how coding agents work through incremental implementation, testing, and failure analysis. It is explicitly NOT intended to clone Pi, Claude Code, or Copilot. Primary success criterion: understanding gained through building/testing core parts ourselves; a useful general-purpose agent is a valuable secondary outcome.

knowledge.title: System non-goals (design doc)
knowledge.text: Initial system will NOT: replace established coding agents; depend on a single LLM provider; read entire repos by default; automatically perform unsafe operations; add RAG/memory/sub-agents/complex planning before the core loop is understood; optimize for max autonomy before reliability; treat every proposed feature as necessary.

knowledge.title: High-level architecture layering
knowledge.text: User -> CLI -> Agent Runtime -> {Context Manager, Agent Loop -> {LLM Interface -> Provider Adapter -> Model API}, Tool Registry -> {File, Search, Command, Git tools}} -> Verification/Evaluation -> Logging/Failure Analysis. Agent loop must stay independent of provider-specific APIs and tool implementation details.

knowledge.title: Explicitly deferred beyond Iteration 1
knowledge.text: Do not build in Iteration 1: RAG, vector DB, embeddings, persistent memory, sub-agents, model routing/auto-switching, MCP, complex planning, complex skill system, plugin marketplace, web UI, autonomous background execution, automatic git push, sophisticated context compaction, large-scale repo indexing. Future iterations (2-12) are: Context, Repository Navigation, Verification, Planning, Skills, Extensions, Git, Sub-Agents, RAG Experiment, Memory, Safety/Evaluation — each gated by evidence from prior iterations, not automatic progression.

knowledge.title: Sandwich ordering in buildMessagesForProvider counters lost-in-the-middle
knowledge.text: LLMs have U-shaped attention: strong recall at context start and end, weak in the middle (Liu et al. 2023, 'Lost in the Middle'). Naively restoring chronological order after context selection places compacted older turns in the middle and recent turns at the end — but critical system/task/fact items can also drift into the middle as history grows. Fix: pin non-removable and critical items (system, task_state, important_fact) to the FRONT; place the most recent maxRecentItems turns at the END; leave older removable turns in the middle where forgetting them is acceptable. Implemented in src/agent/loop.ts buildMessagesForProvider().
knowledge.source: Liu et al. 2023, Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts

knowledge.title: Why Iteration 2's green test suite missed nine real-world bugs
knowledge.text: 86 tests passed before, during and after nine bugs found on first real use. Cause: the mock provider encoded the same assumptions as the code under test. It never set stop_reason (so truncated tool arguments were unrepresentable), always returned well-formed input (so input-keyed stuck detection was never stressed), asserted nothing about message order or id pairing, passed 'operation' explicitly in every edit_file test (so the shape the model actually sends was never exercised), and never produced tied timestamps. Tests verified 'the code does what I think it does' rather than 'the code satisfies the external contract'. Evidence of how hard this is: while actively chasing a KNOWN bug, three successive regression tests passed against known-broken code before one reproduced it. Iteration 3 requirement: a contract-checking fake provider that asserts the real API's invariants on every call, plus property/fuzz tests over failure patterns and interleavings. A brute-force sweep of 128 failure patterns found bug 8's precondition in seconds after six rounds of reasoning failed.

knowledge.title: Tool contracts are a model-facing API
knowledge.text: Three of nine real-world bugs were the harness knowing something it never told the model: the run_command allowlist and the absence of a shell were undocumented in the tool description; edit_file demanded an 'operation' discriminator that no mainstream editing API uses. The model ignored a clear corrective error message ('Use write or replace') three times in a row, because a strong prior beats an error string. Rule: when a model repeatedly ignores corrective text, the contract is wrong, not the model's reading comprehension. Prefer inferring redundant parameters over enforcing them, and state constraints plus the allowlist in the tool description where the model will read them.

knowledge.title: Iteration 1/2 baseline facts at Iteration 3 planning
knowledge.text: 100 tests in 12 files pass and tsc --noEmit is clean on 2026-10-08. IMPL-IT2-1 is still state=paused (its work is exercised by IMPL-IT2-2..7). IMPL-7 is rejected (superseded by IMPL-9). DECISION-c0d3e4f4 (run_command allowlist widened to find, grep, cat, python, npx...) is still NEEDS HUMAN REVIEW. assertInWorkspace is string-prefix based and does not resolve symlinks.
knowledge.source: genesis status; npx vitest run; src/tools/workspace.ts
